newsitem.title: ITALY: Ina warns of weaker 1997 results vs 1996.
newsitem.headline: Ina warns of weaker 1997 results vs 1996.

text.p: Italian insurer Ina warned on Friday that its 1997 results might not be as strong as in 1996 because of the recent fall in interest rates.
"The result from the 1997 accounts could come in at a lower level than that seen in 1996," Ina said in its full 1996 results booklet handed out at a shareholders' meeting.
Ina chalked up a 420.5 billion lire net profit last year, up 6.4 percent on 1995 levels. The gross profit climbed 12.3 percent to 836.9 billion lire.

"Considering the performance of the financial markets, one can foresee that the fall in interest rates will cause a reduction not only of yields on policies tied to funds managed separately, but also to the firm's financial margins," Ina said.

However, Ina managing director Lino Benassi told shareholders that new premiums rose 74 percent in the first four months of 1997 compared with the same period last year, while total premiums rose 20 percent. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
